title: SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts
claim: A hidden scene is reconstructed, turned into a relational state, and searched with LLM-proposed actions and learned rollouts to yield a plan.
layout: 3 rounded panels, left-to-right, arrows between, formulas under each stage
description: Three pastel rounded panels run left to right and are joined by black arrows. The left panel, in purple, is titled 'Hidden-scene Reconstruction from partial observations'. It shows a real RGB shelf photo and a depth map, then a 3D box reconstruction of the shelf with z_t = {s_i} and an object-state box s_i = (μ, σ, p). The middle panel, in blue, is 'Planning State & LLM Action Proposals'. It has a colored relational graph with c_t = (I_c, d_c), an LLM icon with the text 'LLM proposes candidate actions', and A(c_t) shown as colored dots plus a four-way direction arrow. The right panel, in green, is 'Rollouts (MCTS + World Model)'. It has a search tree, rollout state sequences z_t to z_{t+T} drawn as colored cubes, reward boxes (Δvis, Δacc, Δblock, I_invalid), and a brace leading to 'Selected Plan π*'. The eye goes first to the left photos, then follows the arrows.
caption: Overview of SCOUT. From partial RGB-D observations, GHOST reconstructs an object-centric hidden scene representation, which is converted into a relational planning state. An LLM generates structured action proposals, and MCTS with a learned world model evaluates simulated rollouts to guide selection of a multi-step plan.
abstract: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.
